e.etymology: The name of Kenai's older brother in Disney's animated film Brother Bear (2003), set among the Native people of ancient Alaska.

assoc.t: Denahi, Kenai's brother in Disney's Brother Bear

e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Kyaire, Khyaire and Zyaire.
A modern spelling in the family of Eris and Erys. In Greek myth Eris is the goddess of strife, and the name is also carried by a dwarf planet.
From Latin Aurelianus, a derivative of the Roman family name Aurelius, from aureus, golden. Aurelian was the Roman emperor who reunited the empire in the 270s.

e.meaning: fruit of one's hopes and dreams
e.etymology: An old Tagalog word for imagination or the fruit of one's hopes, best known from the phrase hiraya manawari, may your wishes come true.
A pet form of Mary, and sometimes of Margaret, that became a given name in its own right in the 19th century. Mary goes back to Hebrew Miryam, whose meaning is uncertain.
namesakes: Mamie Eisenhower (first lady, wife of Dwight Eisenhower)
Mamie Till-Mobley (civil rights activist, mother of Emmett Till)

e.etymology: A spelling of Kelly, from the Irish surname O Ceallaigh, descendant of Ceallach. The meaning of that old personal name is debated; suggestions include bright-headed and strife.
namesakes: Kellie Pickler (country singer, American Idol alumna)

e.etymology: From a surname, a contraction of Norman French de la Mare, from the pond. In the United States it is also read as Spanish del mar, of the sea.
namesakes: Delmar O'Donnell (escaped convict in O Brother, Where Art Thou?)

e.etymology: A pet form of Christine and Christina, from Latin Christiana, a follower of Christ. Christ is Greek christos, anointed.
namesakes: Chrissy Snow (Suzanne Somers's character on Three's Company)

e.etymology: The English form of Irish Odhran, a diminutive of odhar, dun or sallow. Saint Odhran was a companion of Saint Columba on Iona. In older American use it was also a variant of Oren and Orrin.
A spelling of Julissa, a Latin American elaboration of Julia, the feminine of the Roman family name Julius. The Mexican actress and singer Julissa made it familiar from the 1960s.
From the Italian city of Verona, the setting of Romeo and Juliet. In German-speaking families it has also been a short form of Veronika.

assoc.t: Verona, the Italian city of Romeo and Juliet

e.etymology: An African American coinage joining the prefix De- to Quan, a sound found in 1990s names such as Daquan and Jaquan. A Chinese given name is spelled the same way.
A spelling of Dillon, an Irish surname of Norman origin that is also used as a spelling of Dylan, the Welsh name of a sea figure in the Mabinogion.
The Scandinavian spelling of Annette, a French pet form of Anne, from Hebrew Channah, grace or favor.
A combination of Mary and Anna written as one word. Marianna and Maryanne are related forms.
An American elaboration of Kelly with the ending -lyn. For boys it is also a spelling of Kellen.
Its American peak in 1983 followed child actress Kaleena Kiff of the sitcom Love, Sidney. It matches the sound of Kalina, a Slavic word for the viburnum shrub used as a name in Poland and Bulgaria.
A spelling of Anisa, from Arabic anisa, friendly or companionable, the feminine of Anis.
Sanskrit nidhi, a treasure or store of wealth. In Hindu tradition the nine nidhis are the treasures of Kubera, the god of riches.
The English word once used for the Romani people, shortened from Egyptian because they were wrongly thought to have come from Egypt. As a given name it dates from the 19th century.
namesakes: Gypsy Rose Lee (burlesque star whose memoir became the musical Gypsy)
Gypsy Rose Blanchard (true-crime figure portrayed in The Act)
e.note: Many Romani people regard the word gypsy as an ethnic slur.

assoc.t: gypsy, a word for Romani people now often seen as a slur
Gypsy Rose Blanchard, jailed over her mother's 2015 killing

e.etymology: In Jewish use a Yiddish short form of Kalonymos, a Greek name meaning beautiful name borne by a famous medieval rabbinic family. A separate Hungarian name Kalman goes back to the Irish saint's name Colman, little dove.
The English form of Irish Roisin, little rose. James Clarence Mangan's poem Dark Rosaleen made it a poetic name for Ireland.
A spelling of Ishan, from Sanskrit ishana, lord or ruler, a name of the god Shiva and of the guardian of the northeast.
The English word for a person who traps animals for fur, used as a name in the style of Hunter and Archer. Trapper John is the surgeon in the film and series M*A*S*H.
namesakes: Trapper John McIntyre (surgeon in M*A*S*H and Trapper John, M.D.)

e.etymology: A spelling of Zayna or Zaina, from Arabic zayn, beauty or adornment.
Sanskrit medha, wisdom or intelligence. In Hindu texts Medha is also a name of Saraswati, the goddess of learning.
A Welsh and English surname meaning son of Hugh. Hugh is a Germanic name from hug, mind or spirit, brought to Britain by the Normans.
namesakes: Langston Hughes (poet of the Harlem Renaissance)
Howard Hughes (aviator, film producer and billionaire)

e.etymology: A respelling of Celeste, from Latin caelestis, heavenly, by way of French.
Two names share this spelling: Arabic Samira, a companion in evening conversation, the feminine of Samir, and an Indian name from Sanskrit samira, breeze or wind.
A form of Rosalia and Rosalie, from Latin rosa, rose. It is used in Spanish-speaking families and had some American use in the early 1900s.
The English form of Irish Reamonn, the Irish version of Raymond, a Germanic name made of ragin, counsel, and mund, protection. It is also an Irish surname.
